sanskrit: rathāśvebhanarāṇāṃ ca narāśvebharathaiḥ kṛtam pāṇipādaiś ca śastraiś ca rathaiś ca kadanaṃ mahat
english: A great slaughter of chariots, horses, elephants, and men was wrought by men, horses, elephants, and chariots—by hands and feet, by weapons, and by chariots alike.

sanskrit: tathā tasmin bale śūrair vadhyamāne hate 'pi ca asmān abhyāgaman pārthā vṛkodarapurogamāḥ
english: As that host was being cut down and slain by the brave, the sons of Pṛthā, with Vṛkodara at their head, advanced upon us.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca draupadeyāḥ prabhadrakāḥ sātyakiś cekitānaś ca draviḍaiḥ sainikaiḥ saha
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, the sons of Draupadī, the Prabhadrakas, Sātyaki and Cekitāna, together with the Draviḍa soldiers—

sanskrit: bhṛtā vittena mahatā pāṇḍyāś cauḍrāḥ sakeralāḥ vyūḍhoraskā dīrghabhujāḥ prāṃśavaḥ priyadarśanāḥ
english: and the Pāṇḍyas, the Auḍras, and the Keralas, paid with great wealth—broad-chested, long-armed, tall, and fair to look upon—

sanskrit: āpīḍino raktadantā mattamātaṅgavikramāḥ nānāvirāgavasanā gandhacūrṇāvacūrṇitāḥ
english: crowned with garlands, their teeth reddened, valorous as rutting elephants, clad in robes of many dyes and powdered with fragrant scents,

sanskrit: baddhāsayaḥ pāśahastā vāraṇaprativāraṇāḥ samānamṛtyavo rājann anīkasthāḥ parasparam
english: with swords girded on and nooses in hand, able to ward off charging elephants, sworn to a common death, O king, standing in the ranks shoulder to shoulder—

sanskrit: kalāpinaś cāpahastā dīrghakeśāḥ priyāhavāḥ pattayaḥ sātyaker andhrā ghorarūpaparākramāḥ
english: bearing quivers and bows in hand, long-haired and loving battle—the Andhra footmen of Sātyaki, dreadful in form and prowess.

sanskrit: athāpare punaḥ śūrāś cedipāñcālakekayāḥ karūṣāḥ kosalāḥ kāśyā māgadhāś cāpi dudruvuḥ
english: Then yet other warriors—the Cedis, the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, the Karūṣas, the Kosalas, the Kāśis, and the Māgadhas—rushed forth.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ rathāś ca nāgāś ca pravarāś cāpi pattayaḥ nānāvidharavair hṛṣṭā nṛtyanti ca hasanti ca
english: Their chariots and elephants and choicest footmen, exultant with cries of every kind, danced and laughed for joy.

sanskrit: tasya sainyasya mahato mahāmātravarair vṛtaḥ madhyaṃ vṛkodaro 'bhyāgāt tvadīyaṃ nāgadhūrgataḥ
english: Surrounded by the foremost of mighty elephant-drivers, Vṛkodara, mounted at the head of his elephant, drove into the midst of that great host of thine.

sanskrit: sa nāgapravaro 'tyugro vidhivat kalpito babhau udayādryagryabhavanaṃ yathābhyuditabhāskaram
english: That foremost of elephants, most terrible and duly caparisoned, shone like the lofty mansion of the eastern mount when the risen sun stands upon it.

sanskrit: tasyāyasaṃ varmavaraṃ vararatnavibhūṣitam tārodbhāsasya nabhasaḥ śāradasya samatviṣam
english: Its splendid iron armor, adorned with the choicest gems, gleamed with a radiance equal to the autumn sky aglow with stars.

sanskrit: sa tomaraprāsakaraś cārumauliḥ svalaṃkṛtaḥ caran madhyaṃdinārkābhas tejasā vyadahad ripūn
english: With lance and javelin in hand, fair-crowned and well-adorned, ranging like the noonday sun, he scorched his foes with his splendor.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā dviradaṃ dūrāt kṣemadhūrtir dvipasthitaḥ āhvayāno 'bhidudrāva pramanāḥ pramanastaram
english: Beholding that elephant from afar, Kṣemadhūrti, himself mounted on an elephant, charged exultantly upon the still more exultant one, calling him to combat.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ dvipayor ugrarūpayoḥ yadṛcchayā drumavator mahāparvatayor iva
english: A battle arose between those two elephants of dreadful aspect, like that between two great mountains, tree-clad, met by chance.

sanskrit: saṃsaktanāgau tau vīrau tomarair itaretaram balavat sūryaraśmyābhair bhittvā bhittvā vinedatuḥ
english: Their elephants locked together, those two heroes, piercing each other again and again with lances bright as the rays of the sun, roared mightily.

sanskrit: vyapasṛtya tu nāgābhyāṃ maṇḍalāni viceratuḥ pragṛhya caiva dhanuṣī jaghnatur vai parasparam
english: Drawing their elephants apart, they wheeled in circling courses, and taking up their bows, they smote each other.

sanskrit: kṣveḍitāsphoṭitaravair bāṇaśabdaiś ca sarvaśaḥ tau janān harṣayitvā ca siṃhanādān pracakratuḥ
english: With shouts and the slapping of arms and the twang of arrows on every side, gladdening the warriors, the two raised lion-roars.

sanskrit: samudyatakarābhyāṃ tau dvipābhyāṃ kṛtināv ubhau vātoddhūtapatākābhyāṃ yuyudhāte mahābalau
english: Both skilled and mighty, they fought upon their two elephants—their trunks upraised, their banners tossed by the wind.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyasya dhanuṣī chittvānyonyaṃ vinedatuḥ śaktitomaravarṣeṇa prāvṛṇmeghāv ivāmbubhiḥ
english: Having cut each other's bows, the two roared, raining spears and lances upon one another as the rain-clouds pour down water.

sanskrit: kṣemadhūrtis tadā bhīmaṃ tomareṇa stanāntare nirbibheda tu vegena ṣaḍbhiś cāpy aparair nadan
english: Then Kṣemadhūrti, roaring, pierced Bhīma forcefully between the breasts with a lance, and with six others besides.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenaḥ śuśubhe tomarair aṅgamāśritaiḥ krodhadīptavapur meghaiḥ saptasaptir ivāṃśumān
english: Bhīmasena, his body blazing with wrath, the lances clinging to his limbs, shone like the sun, the seven-horsed, amid the clouds.

sanskrit: tato bhāskaravarṇābham añjogatimayasmayam sasarja tomaraṃ bhīmaḥ pratyamitrāya yatnavān
english: Then Bhīma, with effort, hurled at his foe a lance of straight flight, wrought wholly of iron and bright as the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ kulūtādhipatiś cāpam āyamya sāyakaiḥ daśabhis tomaraṃ chittvā śaktyā vivyādha pāṇḍavam
english: Then the lord of the Kulūtas, drawing his bow, cut down that lance with ten arrows and pierced the Pāṇḍava with a spear.

sanskrit: atha kārmukam ādāya mahājaladanisvanam ripor abhyardayan nāgam unmadaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, taking up a bow that thundered like a great storm-cloud, the furious Pāṇḍava tormented the foe's elephant with his arrows.

sanskrit: sa śaraughārdito nāgo bhīmasenena saṃyuge nigṛhyamāṇo nātiṣṭhad vātadhvasta ivāmbudaḥ
english: That elephant, afflicted by the flood of arrows from Bhīmasena in the fight and held in check, could not stand its ground, like a cloud scattered by the wind.

sanskrit: tām abhyadhāvad dviradaṃ bhīmasenasya nāgarāṭ mahāvāteritaṃ meghaṃ vātoddhūta ivāmbudaḥ
english: The royal elephant rushed upon the elephant of Bhīmasena, as one wind-driven cloud rushes upon another stirred by a mighty gale.

sanskrit: saṃnivartyātmano nāgaṃ kṣemadhūrtiḥ prayatnataḥ vivyādhābhidrutaṃ bāṇair bhīmasenaṃ sakuñjaram
english: Wheeling back his own elephant with effort, Kṣemadhūrti pierced with arrows the charging Bhīmasena together with his elephant.

sanskrit: tataḥ sādhuvisṛṣṭena kṣureṇa puruṣarṣabhaḥ chittvā śarāsanaṃ śatror nāgam āmitram ārdayat
english: Then that bull among men, with a well-aimed razor-headed shaft, cut his foe's bow and tormented the enemy's elephant.

sanskrit: tataḥ khajākayā bhīmaṃ kṣemadhūrtiḥ parābhinat jaghāna cāsya dviradaṃ nārācaiḥ sarvamarmasu
english: Then Kṣemadhūrti struck Bhīma hard with a barbed shaft and smote his elephant with iron arrows in all its vital parts.

sanskrit: purā nāgasya patanād avaplutya sthito mahīm bhīmaseno ripor nāgaṃ gadayā samapothayat
english: Before his elephant could fall, Bhīmasena leaped down and, standing upon the ground, crushed the foe's elephant with his mace.

sanskrit: tasmāt pramathitān nāgāt kṣemadhūrtim avadrutam udyatāsim upāyāntaṃ gadayāhan vṛkodaraḥ
english: As Kṣemadhūrti leaped down from that shattered elephant and came on with uplifted sword, Vṛkodara struck him with his mace.

sanskrit: sa papāta hataḥ sāsir vyasuḥ svam abhito dvipam vajraprarugṇam acalaṃ siṃho vajrahato yathā
english: Slain, his sword still in hand and his life gone, he fell beside his own elephant, like a lion struck by the thunderbolt beside a mountain riven by the same.

sanskrit: nihataṃ nṛpatiṃ dṛṣṭvā kulūtānāṃ yaśaskaram prādravad vyathitā senā tvadīyā bharatarṣabha
english: Beholding slain the glorious king of the Kulūtas, thy army, O bull of the Bhāratas, fled away in distress.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ karṇo maheṣvāsaḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm jaghāna samare śūraḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Karṇa, the great archer, that hero, smote the host of the Pāṇḍavas in battle with his straight-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājaṃs tava putrasya vāhinīm karṇasya pramukhe kruddhā vinijaghnur mahārathāḥ
english: Even so, O king, the Pāṇḍavas, those great car-warriors, enraged, slaughtered the army of thy son before the very face of Karṇa.

sanskrit: karṇo rājan mahābāhur nyavadhīt pāṇḍavīṃ camūm nārācair arkaraśmyābhaiḥ karmāraparimārjitaiḥ
english: Karṇa, O king, the mighty-armed, slew the Pāṇḍava host with iron shafts bright as the sun's rays, polished smooth by the smith.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata karṇena nārācais tāḍitā gajāḥ neduḥ seduś ca mamluś ca babhramuś ca diśo daśa
english: There, O Bhārata, the elephants struck by Karṇa's iron shafts trumpeted and sank down and grew faint and reeled through the ten directions.

sanskrit: vadhyamāne bale tasmin sūtaputreṇa māriṣa nakulo 'bhyadravat tūrṇaṃ sūtaputraṃ mahāraṇe
english: As that host was being slain by the son of the charioteer, O venerable one, Nakula swiftly charged upon the Sūtaputra in the great battle.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tathā drauṇiṃ kurvāṇaṃ karma duṣkaram vindānuvindau kaikeyau sātyakiḥ samavārayat
english: Bhīmasena withstood the son of Droṇa, who was performing deeds hard to achieve, and Sātyaki withstood the Kaikeya brothers Vinda and Anuvinda.

sanskrit: śrutakarmāṇam āyāntaṃ citraseno mahīpatiḥ prativindhyaṃ tathā citraś citraketanakārmukaḥ
english: King Citrasena met the advancing Śrutakarman, and Citra, with his bow of brilliant device and standard, met Prativindhya.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu rājānaṃ dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram saṃśaptakagaṇān kruddho abhyadhāvad dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Duryodhana met King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, while Dhanaṃjaya, enraged, rushed upon the bands of the saṃśaptakas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ kṛpaṃ cātha tasmin vīravarakṣaye śikhaṇḍī kṛtavarmāṇaṃ samāsādayad acyutam
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna met Kṛpa, and in that destruction of the foremost of heroes Śikhaṇḍin closed with the steadfast Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: śrutakīrtis tathā śalyaṃ mādrīputraḥ sutaṃ tava duḥśāsanaṃ mahārāja sahadevaḥ pratāpavān
english: Śrutakīrti met Śalya, and the valiant Sahadeva, son of Mādrī, met thy son Duḥśāsana, O great king.

sanskrit: kekayau sātyakiṃ yuddhe śaravarṣeṇa bhāsvatā sātyakiḥ kekayau caiva chādayām āsa bhārata
english: The two Kekaya brothers covered Sātyaki in battle with a gleaming shower of arrows, and Sātyaki in turn covered the two Kekayas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tāv enaṃ bhrātarau vīraṃ jaghnatur hṛdaye bhṛśam viṣāṇābhyāṃ yathā nāgau pratināgaṃ mahāhave
english: Those two brothers struck that hero hard in the breast, as two elephants strike a rival elephant with their tusks in a great battle.

sanskrit: śarasaṃbhinnavarmāṇau tāv ubhau bhrātarau raṇe sātyakiṃ satyakarmāṇaṃ rājan vivyadhatuḥ śaraiḥ
english: Their armor riven by arrows, those two brothers in the fight pierced Sātyaki, true in deed, with their shafts, O king.

sanskrit: tau sātyakir mahārāja prahasan sarvatodiśam chādayañ śaravarṣeṇa vārayām āsa bhārata
english: But Sātyaki, O great king, laughing, covered those two on every side with a shower of arrows and held them in check, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇau tatas tau tu śaineyaśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ śaineyasya rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ chādayām āsatuḥ śaraiḥ
english: Held back then by the showers of arrows from the grandson of Śini, the two swiftly covered the chariot of the Śaineya with their shafts.

sanskrit: tayos tu dhanuṣī citre chittvā śaurir mahāhave atha tau sāyakais tīkṣṇaiś chādayām āsa duḥsahaiḥ
english: But the grandson of Śūra, having cut their two bright bows in that great battle, then covered them both with sharp and unbearable arrows.

sanskrit: athānye dhanuṣī mṛṣṭe pragṛhya ca mahāśarān sātyakiṃ pūrayantau tau ceratur laghu suṣṭhu ca
english: Then, taking up two other polished bows and great arrows, the two ranged lightly and skillfully, raining their shafts upon Sātyaki.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ muktā mahābāṇāḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavāsasaḥ dyotayanto diśaḥ sarvāḥ saṃpetuḥ svarṇabhūṣaṇāḥ
english: The great arrows loosed by the two, feathered with heron and peacock plumes and adorned with gold, flew on, lighting up all the quarters.

sanskrit: bāṇāndhakāram abhavat tayo rājan mahāhave anyonyasya dhanuś caiva cicchidus te mahārathāḥ
english: A darkness of arrows arose between them in that great battle, O king, and those great car-warriors cut one another's bows.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja sātvato yuddhadurmadaḥ dhanur anyat samādāya sajyaṃ kṛtvā ca saṃyuge kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena anuvindaśiro 'harat
english: Then the Sātvata, O great king, enraged and frenzied for battle, took up another bow and strung it, and in the fight, with a keen razor-headed shaft, struck off the head of Anuvinda.

sanskrit: tacchiro nyapatad bhūmau kuṇḍalotpīḍitaṃ mahat śambarasya śiro yadvan nihatasya mahāraṇe śoṣayan kekayān sarvāñ jagāmāśu vasuṃdharām
english: That great head, weighed down by its ear-rings, fell to the earth like the head of Śambara slain in a great battle, and, withering all the Kekayas, it swiftly passed to the ground.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ śūraṃ bhrātā tasya mahārathaḥ sajyam anyad dhanuḥ kṛtvā śaineyaṃ pratyavārayat
english: Beholding that hero slain, his brother, the great car-warrior, strung another bow and withstood the grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: sa śaktyā sātyakiṃ viddhvā svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ nanāda balavan nādaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Piercing Sātyaki with a spear and with gold-feathered, stone-whetted shafts, he roared a mighty roar and cried, "Stand, stand!"

sanskrit: sa sātyakiṃ punaḥ kruddhaḥ kekayānāṃ mahārathaḥ śarair agniśikhākārair bāhvor urasi cārdayat
english: That great car-warrior of the Kekayas, enraged again, tormented Sātyaki in the arms and breast with arrows shaped like tongues of fire.

sanskrit: sa śaraiḥ kṣatasarvāṅgaḥ sātvataḥ sattvakovidaḥ rarāja samare rājan sapatra iva kiṃśukaḥ
english: His every limb wounded by the arrows, the Sātvata, skilled in courage, shone in the battle, O king, like a kiṃśuka tree in full leaf.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ samare viddhaḥ kekayena mahātmanā kekayaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā vivyādha prahasann iva
english: Sātyaki, pierced in battle by the high-souled Kekaya, pierced the Kekaya in turn with twenty-five shafts, as though laughing.

sanskrit: śatacandracite gṛhya carmaṇī subhujau tu tau vyarocetāṃ mahāraṅge nistriṃśavaradhāriṇau yathā devāsure yuddhe jambhaśakrau mahābalau
english: Taking up their shields decked with a hundred moons, those two strong-armed warriors, bearing excellent swords, shone in the great arena like the mighty Jambha and Śakra in the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: maṇḍalāni tatas tau ca vicarantau mahāraṇe anyonyam asibhis tūrṇaṃ samājaghnatur āhave
english: Then those two, wheeling in circling courses in the great battle, swiftly smote each other with their swords in the fray.

sanskrit: kekayasya tataś carma dvidhā ciccheda sātvataḥ sātyakeś ca tathaivāsau carma ciccheda pārthivaḥ
english: Then the Sātvata cleft the Kekaya's shield in two, and the prince likewise cleft the shield of Sātyaki.

sanskrit: carma cchittvā tu kaikeyas tārāgaṇaśatair vṛtam cacāra maṇḍalāny eva gatapratyāgatāni ca
english: Having cleft the shield set about with hundreds of stars, the Kaikeya ranged in circling courses, advancing and retreating.

sanskrit: taṃ carantaṃ mahāraṅge nistriṃśavaradhāriṇam apahastena ciccheda śaineyas tvarayānvitaḥ
english: As he ranged in the great arena bearing his excellent sword, the grandson of Śini, in haste, cut him down with a back-handed stroke.

sanskrit: savarmā kekayo rājan dvidhā chinno mahāhave nipapāta maheṣvāso vajranunna ivācalaḥ
english: The Kekaya, with his armor, O king, cleft in two in that great battle—that mighty archer fell like a mountain smitten by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: taṃ nihatya raṇe śūraḥ śaineyo rathasattamaḥ yudhāmanyo rathaṃ tūrṇam āruroha paraṃtapaḥ
english: Having slain him in battle, the heroic Śaineya, that best of car-warriors, that scorcher of foes, swiftly mounted the chariot of Yudhāmanyu.

sanskrit: tato 'nyaṃ ratham āsthāya vidhivat kalpitaṃ punaḥ kekayānāṃ mahat sainyaṃ vyadhamat sātyakiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, mounting another chariot duly equipped, Sātyaki once more scattered the great host of the Kekayas with his arrows.

sanskrit: sā vadhyamānā samare kekayasya mahācamūḥ tam utsṛjya rathaṃ śatruṃ pradudrāva diśo daśa
english: That great host of the Kekayas, being slain in the battle, abandoned that hostile chariot and fled through the ten directions.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śrutakarmā mahārāja citrasenaṃ mahīpatim ājaghne samare kruddhaḥ pañcāśadbhiḥ śilīmukhaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Śrutakarman, O great king, enraged, struck King Citrasena in battle with fifty arrows.

sanskrit: abhisāras tu taṃ rājā navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ śrutakarmāṇam āhatya sūtaṃ vivyādha pañcabhiḥ
english: But King Abhisāra, striking Śrutakarman with nine sharp arrows, pierced his charioteer with five.

sanskrit: śrutakarmā tataḥ kruddhaś citrasenaṃ camūmukhe nārācena sutīkṣṇena marmadeśe samardayat
english: Then Śrutakarman, enraged, tormented Citrasena at the head of the army, striking him in a vital spot with a keen iron shaft.

sanskrit: etasminn antare cainaṃ śrutakīrtir mahāyaśāḥ navatyā jagatīpālaṃ chādayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: Meanwhile the illustrious Śrutakīrti covered that guardian of the earth with ninety feathered shafts.

sanskrit: pratilabya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ citraseno mahārathaḥ dhanuś ciccheda bhallena taṃ ca vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: Then, regaining his senses, Citrasena, the great car-warrior, cut his bow with a broad-headed shaft and pierced him with seven arrows.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya vegaghnaṃ rukmabhūṣaṇam citrarūpataraṃ cakre citrasenaṃ śarormibhiḥ
english: Taking up another bow, swift and gold-adorned, he made Citrasena yet more many-hued with his waves of arrows.

sanskrit: sa śaraiś citrito rājaṃś citramālyadharo yuvā yuveva samaśobhat sa goṣṭhīmadhye svalaṃkṛtaḥ
english: Decked with arrows, O king, that youth, wearing a bright garland, shone like a youth well-adorned in the midst of an assembly.

sanskrit: śrutakarmāṇam atha vai nārācena stanāntare bibheda samare kruddhas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Then, enraged, he pierced Śrutakarman between the breasts with an iron shaft in the battle and cried, "Stand, stand!"

sanskrit: śrutakarmāpi samare nārācena samarditaḥ susrāva rudhiraṃ bhūri gairikāmbha ivācalaḥ
english: Śrutakarman too, tormented in the battle by the iron shaft, poured forth abundant blood like a mountain streaming with red ochre.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rudhirāktāṅgo rudhireṇa kṛtacchaviḥ rarāja samare rājan sapuṣpa iva kiṃśukaḥ
english: Then, his limbs smeared with blood and his hue made ruddy by it, he shone in the battle, O king, like a kiṃśuka tree in full flower.

sanskrit: śrutakarmā tato rājañ śatrūṇāṃ samabhidrutaḥ śatrusaṃvaraṇaṃ kṛtvā dvidhā ciccheda kārmukam
english: Then Śrutakarman, O king, charged upon by his foes, warded off the enemy and cut his bow in two.
